transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington I'm Ryland Barton. Officials at Cornell University face
growing criticism over their handling of an alleged rape case in 2024. New York Governor
Kathy Hochul has called for an outside counsel to conduct an independent investigation. NPR's
Brian Mann reports.
Hochul called a woman's account of being drugged and gang-raped at Cornell in 2024 horrifying.
She says there are serious questions and is calling for a transparent, independent review
of the university's response. A local prosecutor says the alleged victim described parts of
the incident as consensual at the time, but potential evidence of violence by seven male
students was only investigated by campus police, not by city police. Ithaca's mayor Robert
Cantelmo has also blasted Cornell's response. In a statement to NPR, Cornell University
says it will work with elected officials to address safety concerns. They didn't say whether
they will approve an independent investigation. Ryan Mann, NPR News, Ithaca, New York.
Former Justice Department Special Counsel Jack Smith was on Capitol Hill today testifying
before lawmakers Smith defended his investigations of President Trump and said he would not be
intimidated by threats of prosecution, as NPR's Ryan Lucas reports.
In his appearance before the Senate Judiciary Committee, Jack Smith said he stands by his
decision to bring charges against President Trump, and that politics played no role in
the investigation.
The charges against President Trump were the result of the evidence.
Evidence of election interference, obstruction, and the mishandling of classified documents.
Republicans repeatedly went after Smith, accusing him of conducting a partisan investigation
to get Trump and Republicans more broadly. Some echoed Trump's calls for Smith himself
to be prosecuted, to which Smith replied,
I will not be silenced by continued threats of prosecution from the president or others.
The more than four-hour hearing ended where it began with a bitter partisan divide.
Ryan Lucas, NPR News, Washington.
OpenAI has launched an AI-enabled bot that its chat GPT users can now access. The bot
called DOTS debuts amid spiraling safety concerns after the company reported similar AI bots
hacked websites and did other things they weren't supposed to during training runs.
NPR's John Ruich reports.
OpenAI's new agent will be able to do a range of tasks for users, from managing email to
fixing computer code. The release fell on the same day that industry leaders met with
President Trump in Washington after a chorus of calls for an AI development slowdown to
make sure humans don't lose control of the technology.
OpenAI President Greg Brockman went to Washington, so CEO Sam Altman could be in San Francisco
for the launch of DOTS at the company's developer conference. Altman says he hopes the AI industry
can forge a sensible middle path between those pushing development at all costs and those
calling for an end to the technology.
John Ruich, NPR News.
Stocks drifted lower on Wall Street today. The S&P 500 fell nearly two-tenths of a percent.
This is NPR.
The Department of Homeland Security has tapped $20 million to pay for campaign-style ads
promoting President Trump. The ads have drawn widespread criticism from Republicans and
Democrats who call them a blatant misuse of taxpayer dollars and likely illegal. Democrats
say Trump's budget director moved the money from Homeland Security to the ad campaign
earlier this month.
Several defendants in the alleged cocaine trafficking ring at Penn State University say they plan
to plead not guilty. Sidney Roach of member station WPSU has more on the latest developments.
Five of the people named in the investigation, including the alleged ring leaders, were originally
scheduled for formal arraignments on Wednesday. But court officials say those defendants have
waived formal arraignments. They'll be back in court in November, and both of the alleged
ring leaders are requesting a jury trial.
Thirteen former Penn State students and one of their parents were arrested last month
before the start of the current fall semester. Pennsylvania's attorney general says cocaine
packaging and sales allegedly happened at two off-campus fraternity houses from 2023
to 2024. For NPR News, I'm Sydney Roach in State College, Pennsylvania.
Chicago native Pope Leo XIV sent a letter of encouragement to the Chicago White Sox
today as they began their postseason series against the Houston Astros. The letter acknowledged
a game on August 11th where the team gave out Pope hats to a sold-out crowd. Leo is
a Sox fan, but the Chicago Cubs have also made it to the playoffs. It's only the fourth
time in history both teams are in the postseason.
This is NPR News from Washington.

topics.text: Cornell University faces criticism over handling of alleged 2024 rape case; Governor Hochul calls for independent investigation
Former Justice Department Special Counsel Jack Smith testifies before Senate Judiciary Committee defending Trump investigations
OpenAI launches DOTS, an AI-enabled bot for ChatGPT users amid safety concerns about AI agent capabilities
Stock market drifts lower; S&P 500 falls nearly two-tenths of a percent
Department of Homeland Security allocates $20 million for campaign-style ads promoting President Trump, drawing criticism
Five defendants in Penn State University cocaine trafficking investigation waive arraignments and plan not guilty pleas
Pope Leo XIV sends letter of encouragement to Chicago White Sox for postseason series against Houston Astros
